sentences.text: Priya Nair is a social worker from adult social care.
Priya Nair spoke to Margaret Doyle on Monday.
Margaret Doyle lives with a heating system that is turned on despite the season.
Margaret Doyle reports that she feels cold and relies on heating to feel warm.
Margaret Doyle lives in a home with a high step that she warns visitors about.
Margaret Doyle has a cat named Biscuit who is 11 years old.
Margaret Doyle was referred to social care by the hospital after discharge.
The purpose of the visit is a needs assessment under the Care Act.
The needs assessment aims to understand how Margaret is managing daily life, what is difficult, what is working, and what matters to her.
Margaret Doyle does not want to be placed in a care home or institution.
The needs assessment is not about placing Margaret in a care home or institution.
The needs assessment is about supporting Margaret in her current home environment.
Margaret Doyle has a quiz programme she watches at 4:00 p.m.
Margaret Doyle said she never gets the answers to the quiz and shouts at the television.
Margaret Doyle said she would allow the social worker to take notes during the assessment.
Margaret Doyle said her handwriting has deteriorated since the last time she wrote anything.
Margaret Doyle said she is comfortable with the social worker sharing information with her GP and any other involved support services.
Margaret Doyle said she has nothing to hide, but added 'mostly'.
Kevin Doyle is Margaret's son.
Kevin Doyle said he would try to come over after finishing an early shift.
Kevin Doyle said he might arrive around half past eleven.
Kevin Doyle said he will 'put his tuppence in' when he visits.
Margaret Doyle's GP is Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery on Church Lane.
Margaret Doyle previously saw Dr Patel at Millbrook Surgery, who retired last summer.
Kevin Doyle expressed concern that the house is too much for Margaret due to stairs and garden.
Kevin Doyle suggested that Margaret might be better off in a sheltered flat or bungalow with a warden on site.
Margaret Doyle stated she is not moving from the house, saying she has been over this with Kevin.
Margaret Doyle said she came to the house as a bride and will not move to a flat with strangers.
Margaret Doyle smokes, but she gave up thirty years ago when Kevin was little.
Margaret Doyle is concerned about money going missing and is unsure where it has gone.
Margaret Doyle says her grandson Jordan, Susan's son, stayed in the UK when his family went to Spain and is twenty-two years old.
Jordan lives in town in a flat with his girlfriend and visits Margaret occasionally.
Jordan sometimes borrows Margaret's bank card to get cash or for himself.
Margaret gave Jordan her bank card number so he could get her shopping when she first came out of hospital.
Margaret says there were a lot of withdrawals from her bank account, more than she asked Jordan for, over the last two months.
Margaret estimates the total amount withdrawn is about six hundred pounds over the last two months.
Margaret says she does not want Jordan to get into trouble because he is young and has had a hard time with his mother going to Spain.
Margaret says she does not know if she gave Jordan permission to use her card, and she cannot remember everything she said.
Margaret says Jordan currently has her bank card.
Margaret says she would be happy for Kevin to know about the money issue and that he will have to know to sort it out.
Margaret says Kevin will be angry when he hears about the money issue.
Kevin Doyle says he is currently out with the bins and is talking to Brenda over the fence.
Kevin Doyle says he put a brick on the bin lid to keep it from blowing off.
Margaret says the bin lid previously went all the way down to number twelve.
Kevin Doyle says Brenda told him a few weeks ago she thought she saw Jordan at the cash machine on the high street by the chemist, with a card, but she wasn't sure it was him.
Kevin Doyle says one of Jordan's old mates' mothers told him Jordan has been in debt with gambling apps on his phone.
Margaret says the information about Jordan being in debt with gambling is just gossip and that Kevin does not know it.
Margaret Doyle is the person being assessed.
The person owns the house and paid it off years ago.
The person receives state pension and Frank's widow's pension (half of Frank's railway pension).
The person has about £9,000 in a building society account, which is for funeral money and grandchildren.
Margaret Doyle is present during the conversation with the social worker and Kevin Doyle.
Kevin Doyle is present during the conversation with the social worker and Margaret Doyle.
Margaret Doyle tells the social worker to 'put it by the phone, love. Biscuit, get off her notes.'
The social worker acknowledges that Kevin wants to sign documents, saying 'he wants to sign them.'
The social worker thanks Margaret for being honest with her during the conversation.
Margaret Doyle said she does not trust herself to carry two cups and a frame.
Margaret Doyle fell on the third of March, a Monday.
Margaret Doyle was in the kitchen when she fell.
Margaret Doyle does not know if she tripped or if she went dizzy.
Margaret Doyle fell from the sink to the floor by the back door.
Margaret Doyle was on the floor for about two hours.
Margaret Doyle could not get up after the fall.
Margaret Doyle tried to turn over but could not put any weight on her wrist.
Margaret Doyle can walk about ten minutes to the shops before the fall.
Margaret Doyle walked to the shops slowly, with a sense of control, and said she would do it.
Margaret Doyle is frightened of going over again after the fall.
Margaret Doyle had a fall in the garden before Christmas, where she sat down on the grass.
Margaret Doyle had a fall in the bathroom in January, where she caught herself on the sink.
Margaret Doyle had a fall in March, which is the third fall in the last six months.
Margaret Doyle has not been referred to a falls clinic or had a falls assessment by her GP.
Margaret Doyle has to go up and down stairs to use the toilet during the day.
Margaret Doyle tries not to drink too much in the afternoons to reduce the need to go to the toilet.
The bedroom and bathroom are upstairs, and the only toilet is upstairs.
There is a rail on the right side of the stairs when going up.
Margaret Doyle goes up the stairs one at a time, holding on with her right hand.
When coming down the stairs, the rail is on the wrong side for her right hand, so she goes down sideways or on her bottom if tired.
Margaret Doyle sometimes goes down the stairs on her bottom, especially when tired, and says it is safer and done in private.
There is only one frame, which is left at the bottom and used by holding onto the wall upstairs.
Margaret Doyle would like a second rail and a second frame for the upstairs stairs.
There are several rugs in the hall and in the living room, which were Frank's mother's or brought back from a holiday in Wales.
The rugs are a trip hazard, especially with a frame.
Kevin has repeatedly told Margaret Doyle about the rugs being a hazard.
Margaret Doyle gets up in the night to use the toilet once or twice.
Margaret Doyle now leaves the landing light on at night to help with nighttime toilet use.
The bathroom is only a few steps from the bedroom.
Margaret Doyle does not currently have a pendant alarm or a fall-detecting button on her person.
Margaret Doyle said she does not want to wear a necklace or look like an 'old woman'.
Margaret Doyle expressed interest in a wrist-worn fall-detecting device that can call for help automatically.
Margaret Doyle reports that she sometimes does not make it to the toilet and leaks when she leaves it too long, especially when going upstairs.
Margaret Doyle wears pads at night and buys them from the supermarket.
Kevin Doyle buys the night pads for Margaret at the big shop.
Margaret Doyle is interested in seeing the continence service, which can assess her and provide free pads if eligible, advice, and exercises.
Margaret Doyle confirms she is happy to receive a referral to the continence service.
Margaret Doyle eats one slice of toast with marmalade and a cup of tea for breakfast.
Margaret Doyle has soup (tin of tomato or chicken) with bread sometimes for lunch or dinner.
In the evening, Margaret Doyle eats yoghurt and sometimes crackers and cheese if she can cut the cheese, but it is hard with one hand.
Margaret Doyle does not cook since the fall and has not turned the cooker on since coming home.
Margaret Doyle cannot lift pans and does not like being in the kitchen due to fear of falling, which happened in the kitchen at the sink.
Margaret Doyle lost nearly a stone since Christmas and her clothes are hanging off her.
Margaret Doyle weighed nine and a half stone all her married life and currently weighs eight stone something.
Margaret Doyle's appetite comes and goes and she does not feel hungry like she used to, especially when alone.
Kevin Doyle does the weekly shopping at the big shop on Sundays.
Brenda gets Margaret milk and bread in the week if she runs out.
Margaret Doyle has a microwave and uses it to cook a jacket potato sometimes.
Kevin Doyle put ready meals in the freezer, but Margaret cannot remove the film off the top.
Margaret Doyle stabs the film with a fork, but it goes everywhere.
Margaret Doyle takes amlodipine (5mg) once a day in the morning for blood pressure.
Margaret Doyle takes alendronic acid (70mg) once a week on Mondays, which must be taken first thing with a large glass of water and she must sit up straight for half an hour.
Margaret Doyle takes paracetamol for her wrist, two tablets up to four times a day, but only takes it once or twice a day if aching.
Margaret Doyle missed two blood pressure tablets (on Tuesday and Thursday morning) last week and is not normally like that.
Margaret Doyle sometimes has trouble opening the tablet box flaps with her wrist and uses a butter knife.
Margaret Doyle has a dosette box (blister pack) delivered every Friday by the chemist on Station Road, which has days marked on it.
Margaret Doyle manages her own money, including paying bills and getting cash out, and bills are auto-debited.
Margaret Doyle has been short on money lately and is not sure where it has gone, and she thinks she may not be keeping track like she used to.
Margaret Doyle said the house is her home where she raised her children.
Margaret Doyle said her garden has Frank's roses and Brenda lives next door.
Margaret Doyle said she wants to stay in her own home for as long as possible.
Margaret Doyle said if she ever had to go into a home, she would want it to be Beechwood because Brenda's sister was there and they were lovely.
Margaret Doyle said she is not going to any home, not by a long chalk.
Kevin Doyle mentioned the back step into the garden is a big drop.
Kevin Doyle mentioned the light at the top of the stairs is on a pull cord, requiring Margaret to reach around for it.
Margaret Doyle said the house is warm enough now because the boiler was replaced last year.
Kevin Doyle said it took him three months to persuade Margaret to replace the boiler.
Margaret Doyle reports her memory is generally okay, though she sometimes forgets where she has put her glasses.
Margaret Doyle can still recall all the kings and queens.
The person has experienced three falls: one on the third of March, and two before that.
The person is unable to bathe properly and wash her hair due to difficulty with mobility and confidence.
The person takes up to an hour to get dressed, which wears her out.
The person is unable to prepare proper meals and eats very little.
The person has lost nearly a stone in weight.
The person has missed some of her tablets.
The person is on her own a lot and feels lonely and more low than usual.
The person is concerned about falling and the safety of the kitchen environment.
The person would like to be able to cook a proper dinner now and then, such as mince and potatoes.
The person wants to stay in her own home, specifically in the current house, with Biscuit (a pet or family member).
The person wants to have a proper bath and wash her hair.
The person wants to return to the lunch club, seeing Joan and Pat.
The person does not want to be frightened of falling or of the kitchen.
The person would like to see her roses (Frank's roses) come out this summer and be well enough to go out and look at them.
The person does not currently receive Attendance Allowance, despite being over state pension age and needing help with personal care.
The person is eligible for Attendance Allowance, as it is not means-tested and based on need for personal care.
The person is not aware of her eligibility for Attendance Allowance.
The person would rather pay a small amount and stay in her home than anything else.
The social worker will refer the person to occupational therapy for a bath lift, a board, a second rail on the stairs, a second frame for upstairs, and a check on the back step and
The occupational therapy waiting list is currently about three weeks.
Margaret Doyle advises the social worker to 'mind how you go in that wind' and to 'have a think about the umbrella.'
The social worker states she will be fine and says goodbye to Kevin.
Margaret Doyle says 'Bye love. Mind the step.'
Margaret Doyle did not tell her GP about the two falls in the garden and bathroom.
Margaret Doyle told Kevin about the garden fall because he found mud on her coat.
Margaret Doyle said a fall-detecting device might have been useful on March 3rd, when she fell and lay there for two hours.
Kevin Doyle says he thinks they should call the police because Jordan is taking Margaret's money, which he says is theft, even if it's family.
Margaret says she does not want the police involved and will not have them come to the house for Jordan.
Margaret says she wants Jordan to stop and for her to get her card back.
The social worker says she will raise the issue of unauthorised withdrawals as a safeguarding concern because it sounds like someone may be taking Margaret's money without her full
The social worker explains that the safeguarding concern does not mean Jordan will be arrested.
The social worker says she will pass Margaret's account details and concerns to the council's safeguarding adults team for review.
The social worker says the safeguarding team will focus on Margaret's wishes: not involving police and wanting Jordan to stop and get the card back.
Margaret says she does not want the police involved, and confirms this is not about police involvement.
The social worker says that if there was a risk to someone else, police involvement would be considered, but only if Margaret decided or if there was a risk to another person.
The person may have to contribute financially to ongoing care if it is arranged by the council, depending on income and savings.
The house is not counted in the financial assessment for care at home.
The social worker will make a safeguarding referral about the card (a financial card) this afternoon.
The safeguarding team will contact Margaret directly after the referral.
The social worker will refer the person for a telecare alarm (Careline watch) that detects falls.
Margaret Doyle is concerned about a step in the home environment, indicating a risk of falling.
Kevin Doyle has a key to the house and can enter the property.
Kevin Doyle is Margaret’s son and is present during the assessment.
Kevin Doyle says he came straight from work and is a bit tired.
Margaret Doyle says Kevin smells of the warehouse.
Kevin Doyle visits Margaret mainly on Sundays, sometimes midweek if he is on early shifts.
Kevin Doyle lives in Northampton, 40 minutes away by car.
Kevin Doyle works shifts at a warehouse.
Kevin Doyle has two teenagers and his wife works.
Margaret Doyle said Kevin does more than he should.
Margaret Doyle has a daughter, Susan, who lives in Alicante, Spain.
Susan moved to Spain with her husband eight years ago.
Margaret Doyle said Susan calls every week, on Sunday nights, and visits in summer.
Margaret Doyle said Susan was unable to visit after the fall due to time constraints.
Kevin Doyle said Susan was on the phone to him every day during the fall.
Margaret Doyle said Susan was worried sick during the fall.
Brenda, who lives next door, visits Margaret most days for a minute.
Margaret Doyle said Brenda knocks on the wall in the morning and she knocks back as a signal that she is okay.
Margaret Doyle said Brenda is 76 years old and has knee problems, so she cannot lean on her.
Margaret Doyle used to attend a lunch club at St Michael's church hall every Wednesday.
Margaret Doyle said the lunch club had a cooked dinner, pudding, and activities like bingo or quizzes or guest talks.
Margaret Doyle said there was a man who brought real owls, one of which sat on her arm.
The social worker will send the Attendance Allowance form and financial assessment form to the family.
Kevin Doyle is the son of Margaret Doyle and is involved in the interaction with the social worker.
Kevin Doyle says 'Cheers, Priya. See you on the fifteenth.'
The next scheduled meeting with the social worker is on the 15th.
